subject: Eval sprint safety buffer request — temporary dedicated slice
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-11-10T09:15:00-08:00
Subject: Eval sprint safety buffer request — short duration

Hi Logan / Kimberly,

We have an internal evaluation sprint for Helios Labs that runs Nov 20–29 (10 days). Product needs a short-term dedicated slice as a safety buffer for nightly regression/eval runs: these are heavy KV-cache warmups and large-context generation tests. We want to avoid noisy cross-tenant interference for the duration.

Initial asks:
- Dedicated slice: 6 x 80GB GPUs (or equivalent) for Nov 20 00:00 UTC — Nov 29 23:59 UTC
- Soft autoscale: allow +2 GPUs for short bursts (max 8) but prefer capacity guaranteeing baseline 6 non-preemptible
- Data isolation: logs may contain customer test inputs; treat as standard pilot data (no special enclave)
- Rollout plan: can run during business hours only, with nightly long runs from 22:00–04:00 UTC

Attachments: sprint_runbook.pdf (run plan), workload_profile.csv (expected token/sec, seq lengths).

We know this is a tight ask close to the calendar — nominal reason: cross-team model sweep + regression coinciding with a spike in eval jobs.

Can you confirm feasibility and cost center to bill? If dedicated carve is not possible, what fallback (preemptible burst lanes or prioritized queue placement) would you recommend?

Thanks,
Naomi
---
Naomi Feldman
Product Manager, Evaluation Programs
Redwood Inference

From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-11-10T11:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Eval sprint safety buffer request — short duration

Thanks Naomi — tagging this for capacity intake. A couple of clarifying items before I raise to the allocator team:

1) Can you confirm the sustained token/sec and peak simultaneous sessions? workload_profile.csv has a per-run line but we need 1) baseline TPS and 2) expected peak concurrent hosts.
2) Is the quality of output allowed to use a quantized variant (int8) during night runs? If we can use a quantized model, we can shrink the required GPU count by ~25%.
3) Billing: please confirm the internal project string (so we can assign commit). Who owns the Helios pilot budget?
4) Do you need network isolation or KMS integration for artifacts?

I will tentatively open a Reservation Request (JIRA-HELIOS-9421) once we have these answers. I also need Kimberly's nod for a temporary autoscale exception — we typically don't allow baseline non-preemptible for short pilots during peak Q4 demand.

- Logan
Logan Wright
Capacity & Allocations, Redwood Inference

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-11-11T08:27:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Eval sprint safety buffer request — short duration

Thanks Logan — answers inline below and I also attached an updated workload_profile.csv with per-hour peaks: see the second tab.

1) Baseline: ~1.8M tokens/hour across the fleet (~140 TPS sustained during business hours). Peak concurrent sessions: 22 (parallel long context sweeps). Peak windows are 22:00–02:00 UTC where token throughput jumps ~2.5x.
2) Quantization: acceptable for the nightly regression runs (we run quality checks on a small holdout set beforehand). For the daytime interactive validation we want FP16. So we need mixed setup: baseline day FP16, nights quantized.
3) Billing: charge to HELIOS-PILOT (internal project id). Finance contact is Priya N. (cc'd separately if needed).
4) Network/KMS: no extra KMS integration required. Standard VPC controls are fine.

If it's helpful, we can reduce baseline to 5 GPUs if we commit to quantized models for two of the 10 nights — but prefer 6 non-preemptible for stability.

Naomi

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>
Cc: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-11-13T14:10:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Eval sprint safety buffer request — short duration

Naomi / Logan,

We can approve a temporary carve, with constraints. Summary of approved reservation: 
- Reservation id: RESV-2025-1147
- Baseline: 6 x 80GB GPUs (non-preemptible)
- Burst headroom: autoscale soft-limit +2 GPUs (max 8) permitted for 30-minute bursts only; any sustained bursts >30m will be throttled to baseline
- Window: 2025-11-20T00:00:00Z — 2025-11-29T23:59:00Z
- Billing: HELIOS-PILOT (project string confirmed)
- Conditioning:
  * Nightly regression may use quantized model variants — ops to pin the model family to avoid kernel churn
  * Daytime validation runs must use FP16 variant only
  * SRE must sign off on runbook updates (link: https://drive.redwood.ai/teams/infra/helios-pilot/runbook) before carve becomes active
  * Any extension beyond Nov 29 requires a formal re-request 72 hours before end date

Attachments: reservation_agreement.md (terms + billing assignment).

Operational notes: Logan, please update the autoscale policy on the reservation to soft-mode and add a preemptible fallback lane for the burst headroom in case inter-region capacity contention appears. David, I'll need you in the loop to reconcile quotas against other Q4 commitments.

Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Capacity Programs Manager
Redwood Inference

From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-11-15T17:40:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Eval sprint safety buffer request — short duration

All — reservation created and scheduled. Quick summary and next steps:

- RESV-2025-1147 is now live in the allocator for Nov 20–29. Reservation owner: HELIOS-PILOT.
- Autoscale mode set to soft; burst headroom policy added with 30-minute sliding window.
- I created an ops checklist (JIRA-HELIOS-9421) with tasks: model pin, SRE runbook signoff, billing tag; assigned to David for quota reconciliation.
- If you see any preflight failures on Nov 19 runs, escalate to infra-oncall immediately and tag RESV-2025-1147.

I'll post the final reservation link and cost estimate after the allocator finishes the commit (should be by end of day tomorrow).

- Logan
notes: This thread covers a short-term dedicated reservation request for an internal pilot/eval sprint and the decision path (clarifying workload, mixed-precision strategy, and conditional carve approval)
Reservation id referenced in the thread: RESV-2025-1147
